alloy.preparation: Arc melted pure metals (99.99 wt%) on water-cooled copper hearth (ABJ-900) under Ti-gettered argon at vacuum stated as at least 0.01 Torr; remelted at least four times. Rectangular cast ingots annealed at 1250 °C for 50 h and water quenched, then forged at 1250 °C with 50% reduction to about 10 mm thickness, and air cooled. Tested in as-forged condition. For polarization, cut to 1 × 1 × 0.5 cm, cold mounted in epoxy with copper-line back contact and 1 cm² exposed; ground through 200–2000-grit SiC, then cleaned with alcohol, acetone and deionized water.
alloy.microstructure: Single FCC A1 solid solution, homogeneous elemental distribution and randomly oriented equiaxed grains about 50 µm.

test_solution.preparation: The Figure 11 comparison is explicitly scoped to 3.5 wt.% NaCl. Numerical pH, chloride-ion concentration, solvent and gas conditioning are not supplied.

test_method.procedure_description: Three-electrode cell with specimen working, SCE reference and Pt-sheet auxiliary; PARSTAT 2263. Tests at reported room temperature 20 ± 2 °C. Free corrosion for 30 min to quasi-stationary OCP, then scan from −0.25 V versus OCP until current density reaches 1 mA/cm². Work-function/SEM/AFM polishing protocols and calculated phase-equilibrium temperatures are not the electrode procedure.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Ep is the potential at which current density exceeds 100 µA/cm² and increases continually, used as an index of localized-corrosion resistance. This differs from the 1 mA/cm² scan endpoint. Al0.7 specimens also exhibit selective dissolution.
